n: As death approaches, David gives Solomon his final charge — a father’s last instructions to a son who must now lead God’s people.
“I go the way of all the earth” — David speaks calmly of his death. He urges Solomon to be strong and act with maturity and courage.

f.w: I go the way of all the earth

n: The heart of David’s charge: obey God’s law as given through Moses, and you will prosper. True success flows from faithfulness.

f.w: keep the charge of the LORD thy God

f.g: God’s solemn witnesses or covenant declarations.

n: David reminds Solomon that God’s promise of a lasting dynasty depends on his descendants walking faithfully before God with all their heart and soul.

f.w: with all their heart and with all their soul

n: David turns to unfinished business. Joab murdered two commanders, Abner and Amasa, in peacetime as if in war, staining himself — and David’s reign — with innocent blood.

f.w: shed the blood of war in peace
f.g: Killed men in peacetime as though it were battle — murder.

n: David asks Solomon to use his wisdom so that Joab doesn’t die peacefully in old age. Unpunished bloodshed was believed to defile the land and the king’s house.
In contrast, Barzillai’s sons are to be honored with a place at the king’s table, in gratitude for their father’s loyalty during Absalom’s revolt.
David brings up Shimei, who cursed him bitterly. David had sworn not to kill him personally.
But David’s oath does not bind Solomon. Using his wisdom, Solomon is to deal with Shimei’s guilt. A curse against the Lord’s anointed was a serious crime under the law.
David dies and is buried in the City of David. Peter mentions his tomb as still known in Jesus’ day.
David reigned forty years: seven in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.
Solomon takes David’s throne, and his kingdom is firmly established — a theme this chapter repeats.
Adonijah approaches Bath-sheba, Solomon’s mother. Wary, she asks if he comes in peace.
He says he has something to ask of her.
Adonijah claims the kingdom should have been his and that all Israel expected him to reign — an exaggeration — but admits the Lord gave it to Solomon.

f.w: it was his from the LORD

n: He has one request and asks her not to refuse.
He asks her to request Abishag, David’s nurse, as his wife. Bath-sheba may not see the danger, but marrying a king’s companion could be read as a claim to his throne.
Bath-sheba agrees to speak to the king for him.
Solomon honors his mother: he rises, bows, and seats her on a throne at his right hand. In Israel, the king’s mother held a position of great dignity.

f.g: The queen mother (gebirah) was an influential figure in Judah’s royal court.

n: She calls it a small request, and Solomon promises not to refuse her.
She asks that Abishag be given to Adonijah as his wife.
Solomon immediately sees through it: why not ask for the kingdom itself for his older brother and his supporters, Abiathar and Joab? He views it as a renewed bid for the throne.

f.w: ask for him the kingdom also

n: Solomon swears a solemn oath that Adonijah’s request will cost him his life.

f.w: God do so to me, and more also
f.g: A standard oath: may God punish me severely if I don’t carry this out.

n: Solomon cites God’s faithfulness in establishing him as king and building him a “house” — a dynasty — as promised. He orders Adonijah’s execution.

f.w: who hath made me an house, as he promised

n: Benaiah carries out the sentence. Adonijah had been warned that any further disloyalty would mean death.
Abiathar, who supported Adonijah, deserves death, but Solomon spares him because he carried the ark and suffered alongside David. He is banished to his estate in Anathoth.

f.g: A priestly town in Benjamin, a few miles northeast of Jerusalem; later Jeremiah’s hometown.

f.w: afflicted in all wherein my father was afflicted

n: Removing Abiathar from the priesthood fulfills the prophecy against the house of Eli, from which Abiathar descended. God’s word, spoken about a century before, comes to pass.

f.w: the word of the LORD, which he spake concerning the house of Eli

n: Joab hears the news and flees to the tabernacle, grabbing the horns of the altar for sanctuary. He had stayed loyal through Absalom’s revolt but backed Adonijah.

f.w: caught hold on the horns of the altar

n: Solomon is told where Joab is and sends Benaiah to execute him.
Joab refuses to leave the altar, saying he will die there. Benaiah reports back to the king.
Solomon orders Benaiah to do as Joab said. The law gave no sanctuary at the altar to a deliberate murderer, and removing Joab cleanses David’s house from bloodguilt.
Joab’s guilt returns on his own head: he killed two men more righteous than himself without David’s knowledge.

f.w: my father David not knowing thereof

n: The guilt for their blood rests on Joab’s line, but Solomon prays that David’s house and throne will have the Lord’s peace forever.

f.w: peace for ever from the LORD

n: Benaiah kills Joab, and he is buried at his family property in the wilderness of Judah.
Solomon promotes Benaiah to army commander and makes Zadok the leading priest. Zadok’s family would hold the high priesthood for generations.
Solomon puts Shimei under a kind of house arrest: he must live in Jerusalem and never leave.

f.w: go not forth thence any whither
f.g: Do not go anywhere outside the city.

n: If Shimei crosses the Kidron Valley — the road toward his home in Bahurim — he will die, and it will be his own fault.

f.w: thy blood shall be upon thine own head

n: Shimei agrees the terms are fair and lives in Jerusalem for a long time.
Three years later, two of Shimei’s slaves run away to Achish, king of Gath.
Shimei saddles his donkey, goes to Gath, and brings them back — ignoring his oath.
Solomon learns that Shimei left Jerusalem and returned.
Solomon reminds him that he swore by the Lord to stay, and agreed the terms were good.
Why did he break his oath before the Lord and the king’s command?
Solomon reminds Shimei of the evil he did to David. Now the Lord is bringing his wickedness back on his own head.

f.g: Aware of, sharing in the secret of.

n: But Solomon himself will be blessed, and David’s throne established forever before the Lord.

f.w: the throne of David shall be established before the LORD for ever

n: Benaiah executes Shimei. The chapter closes with its theme: the kingdom is now firmly established in Solomon’s hand. The violent loose ends of David’s reign have been resolved.

f.w: the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon
